blocks.text: I can’t recommend a complete award journey from these results: the award evidence consists of incomplete leads, not verified end-to-end itineraries. The cash search does give a separate January 1 SFO–Bangkok baseline; it is useful for comparing the cash option, but it is not an award recommendation.
A direct-route cash baseline for January 1—not an award itinerary.

If you’re looking at awards for January 1, the two SFO–Bangkok leads point in different directions: United offers the lower quoted mileage than Aeroplan, while Alaska’s lead has the lowest mileage among these direct-route examples. These are program-specific figures, not directly comparable currencies, and none supplies a flight schedule or confirms a complete, bookable trip.
A United economy lead for SFO–Bangkok on January 1.

blocks.text: There is also a January 1 business-class lead from Taipei to Bangkok, which could matter if you are willing to consider a positioning itinerary. It does not cover the SFO–Taipei portion, so it is not a substitute for a complete SFO–Bangkok journey; arranging separate flights would add cost and connection risk.
A business-class award lead for Taipei–Bangkok on January 1, not the requested origin-to-destination journey.

blocks.text: Treat all award observations as leads rather than confirmed availability: they do not establish schedules, workable connections, protected transfers, or complete trip pricing. The quoted cash amounts and taxes have unknown price scope, so they should not be treated as a confirmed party total. The Taiwan-route search was partial, and detailed award searches for SFO–Bangkok were omitted; these dated observations are not real-time results.
